Windows one-file release of VBA Add-in Editor. The ZIP contains `VBAAddinEditor.exe` and its SHA-256 checksum file.

## Import a button from another add-in

**Ribbon → Import Button from Another Add-in…** copies a ribbon button, and the macros behind it, from another `.xlam`, `.ppam` or `.pptm` into the file you have open. The other add-in is only read, so it can stay loaded in Office.

- Pick a button, toggle, menu or whole group, and where it goes: one of your groups, menus or tabs, or a new group on one of your tabs.
- A preview shows everything that will be added and renamed before you click **Import**.
- One **Undo** reverts the whole import. Nothing is written until **Save File**.

### What comes along

- Every macro the button runs, and everything those macros call, followed through the whole chain. That includes constants, module variables, `Declare` statements (with their `#If VBA7` blocks), Types, Enums, and macros started by name with `Application.Run`, `OnTime`, `OnKey` or `OnAction`.
- Class modules the code uses, copied whole with their attributes.
- The button's custom icon, if it has one.

Each module that code comes from becomes one new module in your add-in, with its `Option` lines, so Private names keep their meaning.

### Works with both add-ins loaded

- The button's macros, and macros started by name, always get a new name with a suffix: `_<your file's name>` by default, editable in the dialog. No macro name is then shared between the two add-ins.
- Other modules, procedures, variables and control ids are renamed only when your add-in already uses the name.
- Every reference is updated to match: calls, `Module.Proc`, control ids in strings such as `InvalidateControl "btnX"`, and `"'Other.xlam'!Proc"` strings, which then name your file.
- Code your add-in already has, identical character for character, is reused instead of copied again.
- If the code keeps the ribbon in an `IRibbonUI` variable, a small `RibbonLoaded…` Sub that sets it is added. Your ribbon's `onLoad` calls it, or it becomes the `onLoad` when you have none.
- Attributes that would stop the ribbon loading in the new place are left out: `size` outside a group, `description` outside a menu, and `insertAfter…` / `insertBefore…`.

### Limits

- The import is refused if the code uses a UserForm your add-in does not have. This editor cannot copy form layouts, so import the form in the VBA editor first. It is also refused if either project is password-protected.
- The summary lists what to check afterwards: library references your add-in lacks (add them in **Tools → References**), sheets of the other add-in the code reads, and imports between Excel and PowerPoint.
- Your add-in needs ribbon XML already; creating a ribbon from scratch is not supported yet.
- A macro whose name is built while the code runs, such as `Application.Run "Do" & n`, cannot be followed.

The imported code was checked in Excel with both add-ins loaded at once: the original and the imported macro each ran in their own add-in. The copied Declare, Type, Enum and class code compiled and ran. Seeing the imported button on a visible ribbon has not been checked yet, so please try a first import on a copy.

## Notes

- This is a development build, built and tested on GitHub's Windows runner. It has not been through the live Excel/PowerPoint qualification matrix. Keep the automatic backup on.
- Known bug: a module whose code starts with a blank line fails save verification ("Body mismatch"). The original file is left untouched; remove the leading blank line and save again.
- Password-protected VBA projects remain read-only.
